title: ‘The Assassin(s)’ Review: A Riveting South Korean Popcorn Thriller About a Real Assassination
description: Hur Jin-ho’s star-studded “The Assassin(s)” turns the holes in a public investigation into an imaginative mystery along the lines of Oliver Stone’s
body:
Hur Jin-ho’s star-studded “The Assassin(s)” turns the holes in a public investigation into an imaginative mystery along the lines of Oliver Stone’s “JFK.” Like Stone’s provocative thriller, Hur crafts a clockwork political saga sure to spark curiosities about the attempted assassination of strongman South Korean prime minister Park Chung-hee in 1974, which resulted in the death of his wife, first lady Yuk Young-soo, as well as a young bystander.
	

	The film ties these events into larger concerns surrounding freedom of the press and some inventive government conspiracies. Your mileage may vary when it comes to the extent of these fabrications, even though “The Assassin(s)” begins with a disclaimer hinting at its own fictions. Regardless, its drama is solid and propulsive, beginning with a group of journalists being harangued by the KCIA (Korean Central Intelligence Agency) for publishing troublesome investigations en route to the botched assassination (intentionally so, according to the film’s internal logic). 

	The three most prominent characters are charismatic and sympathetic in equal measure. Two of them are journalists at the Dong-sung Daily, who mount a heroic stand against government forces at a time of severe censorship. Fiery rookie Young-il (Lee Min-ho) — the younger brother of a connected official — is assigned to cover the prime minister’s Liberation Day speech when the shooting goes awry, leading him to witness the events first-hand. The older, world-weary Jae-hwan (Park Hae-il) leads the City Desk, and investigates the event from a distance with the help of his police source, diligent detective Cheol-goo (Yoo Hai-jin). 
	

	The local policeman isn’t just present on the day, but tries to stop the eventual assassin from entering the auditorium for the prime minister’s speech, until he’s directed otherwise by senior authorities. He’s punished regardless by suits who refuse to listen, galvanizing the characters’ investigations into a larger collusion.

	With a murderer’s row of supporting actors — like Park Hoon as a vicious KCIA goon harassing the Dong-sung workers, and Bae Seong-woo as the paper’s editor, trapped between maintaining journalistic integrity and bowing to censorious demands — the film establishes and unravels its drama at lightning speed. Hur judiciously constructs scene after scene that pulls and pushes the various probes closer to and further from the mysterious truth, which feels at once obscured and hidden in plain sight. As the puzzle pieces shift slowly into place, these revelations are jaw-dropping (once again, in their highly fictitious context), leading to a journalistic urgency.

	Like any good cover-up movie, “The Assassin(s)” luxuriates in process and proficiency, following its cops and journalists sleuthing about to ask questions and peek at documents, poking their noses where they shouldn’t. It’s an invigorating kind of cinema, and Hur knows exactly how and when to tighten the screws, bringing his characters face to face with critical dangers, and with identities shrouded in mystery. These unspool in the form of action scenes where the stakes aren’t just personal safety, but the larger ideals of a nation under political suppression. Its tale of a Zainichi assassin (an ethnic Korean in Japan), as well as fraying political tensions between the North and South, take its characters far and wide, in a follow-the-money treasure hunt dangerously close to the halls of power.

	To spin total concoctions into something so riveting is — for better or worse — an admirable cinematic skill, one Hur uses to turn a tale of forensic malfeasance into mass entertainment of considerable quality. (At Toronto, where the film premiered, it was the second runner-up for the International People’s Choice Award.) There are unanswered questions about these events to this day, and while “The Assassin(s)” isn’t the answer anyone was looking for, the movie taps into a national mood of frustrated anti-authoritarianism, while playing melodramatic tribute to those willing to speak truth to power. The result is rousing, popcorn-munching fun.

schema.headline: ‘The Assassin(s)’ Review: A Riveting South Korean Popcorn Thriller About a Real Assassination

title: Ke Huy Quan Says His $100,000 ‘Indiana Jones’ Residual Check Was ‘Life-Changing’ As a Child Actor: It ‘Didn’t Make Any Sense’
description: Ke Huy Quan shared in his new memoir, “Never Say Die,” the feeling of receiving his first residual check of $100,000 for “Indiana Jones and the Temp
body:
Ke Huy Quan shared in his new memoir, “Never Say Die,” the feeling of receiving his first residual check of $100,000 for “Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom” as a child actor.

	Because Quan was just 12 years old when he booked the role of Short Round in the 1984 film (his first major role as an actor), he didn’t realize he would receive residuals in addition to his base pay.


	“One afternoon, I walked into the kitchen and found my parents standing together at the table,” Quan wrote in the memoir via Entertainment Weekly. “Mom was holding an envelope with my name printed across it. Dad had the papers that had been inside.”
	

	He continued, writing, “They were both smiling, the kind of smile that comes from surprise and disbelief mixed together. They handed everything to me. It was a check from Lucasfilm. It was for almost $100,000, an amount that didn’t make any sense to me.”


	“Back then, almost no actors got a piece of a movie’s profits,” Quan continued. “Even today, only the biggest stars do. That a kid like me, making his first film, would be included in something like that was unheard of. And ‘Temple of Doom’ wasn’t some small movie no one was expected to see. It was the sequel to a massive hit, a movie everyone knew would make a lot of money. That made their gesture even more generous.”

	Quan noted that the “small share was life-changing for my family.”

	As a child, Quan also starred in Richard Donner’s 1985 film “The Goonies” as Data. He returned to the spotlight in 2023 after decades for “Everything Everywhere All at Once,” winning the Oscar for best supporting actor. His memoir, released Tuesday, details his early life fleeing Vietnam with his father, time in refugee camps, his life as a child actor and his triumphant return to the screen.

schema.headline: Ke Huy Quan Says His $100,000 ‘Indiana Jones’ Residual Check Was ‘Life-Changing’ As a Child Actor: It ‘Didn’t Make Any Sense’

title: Ben Affleck Almost Cast Ex-Wife Jennifer Garner in ‘Animals’ Before Deciding ‘We Don’t Wanna Do That’: ‘You Just Get Baggage’
description: Ben Affleck originally wanted to cast his ex-wife, Jennifer Garner, as the leading lady in his latest directorial effort, “Animals,” until a schedul
body:
Ben Affleck originally wanted to cast his ex-wife, Jennifer Garner, as the leading lady in his latest directorial effort, “Animals,” until a scheduling conflict meant he’d have to step into the role opposite her.  

	“I thought, God, Jen Garner would be amazing for this role,” he told Entertainment Weekly. “It also has the added benefit of, like, both of us will see our kids more because we do a week and a week and back and forth. I thought, well, we can coordinate our schedules around it.” He also noted that he thought Garner could “bring something interesting that she hasn’t [done], that I kind of know she can do, that I don’t think she had a chance to do in one movie.” 
	

	Initially, Matt Damon was attached to star as Mark Kimball, the male lead. But because of scheduling conflicts and another film in the same genre slated for a similar release window, Affleck tabled the film two weeks before production was set to begin. When it was time to revive “Animal,” Damon was set to star in another project: “The Odyssey.” 


	“Matt was unfortunately doing another lesser film, obviously, with Odyssey,” Affleck joked. “He chose a smaller director and a smaller film and a smaller role for his career, and I think he’s gonna suffer for it. He’ll regret this choice.” 

	Affleck stepped in for Damon, and the former couple ultimately decided they didn’t want the “baggage” that would come with the on-screen pairing: “I talked to Jen, and she was like, ‘We don’t wanna do that. You just get baggage,’” he said.

	“I would love to work with her, frankly,” he continued. “She’s fabulous, and we’re really good friends, and I’m profoundly grateful to her, and we have a great thing. I still would wanna work with her in the future, but what you don’t wanna do is take the audience’s baggage and have it work against you, you know?”
	

	Co-written by Affleck, Connor O. McIntyre and Billy Ray, “Animals” stars Affleck as a Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose son is kidnapped, giving him and his wife, Abigail (Kerry Washington), a few hours to come up with the ransom money.

	“Animals” premieres on Oct. 9 on Netflix.

schema.headline: Ben Affleck Almost Cast Ex-Wife Jennifer Garner in ‘Animals’ Before Deciding ‘We Don’t Wanna Do That’: ‘You Just Get Baggage’

title: ’60 Minutes’ Patrick Clancy Interview Provides a Surprisingly Thoughtful Take on Much-Watched Trial
description: Credit is merited when it’s due: CBS News’ newly minted “60 Minutes” correspondent Ross Douthat landed a thoughtful, emotional interview with the pe
body:
Credit is merited when it’s due: CBS News’ newly minted “60 Minutes” correspondent Ross Douthat landed a thoughtful, emotional interview with the person who may have elicited more speculation than anyone else this year.

	Patrick Clancy is the grieving father of three children killed in January 2023 by his then-wife, Lindsay Clancy. (During the criminal trial about whether Lindsay was sane or not when she committed the crime, she testified to killing them while in the throes of post-partum psychosis. Because of one holdout juror who’s proclaimed he was convinced of her guilt, the Massachusetts judge reluctantly had to declare a mistrial earlier this month.) As the “60 Minutes” segment points out, Patrick Clancy has been the subject of predictably intense scrutiny, with much of the TikTok commentariat convinced he did the deed.
	

	Whether or not Patrick Clancy came off as credible is up for debate. To this viewer (someone who has literally never used TikTok and is generally skeptical of citizen journalism) he was the picture of bereavement; to others, it may be a judgment call. But he read to me like a person who’d been through, to say the very least, a horrible ordeal, doing the thing that he needed to do to silence the relentless commentary — if that could even be possible. And “60 Minutes” deserves credit for letting him share his side of things after social media has adjudicated his guilt. 


	Douthat, until recently slotted into the New York Times opinion desk as one of the providers of that newspaper’s conservative perspective, can count this as his first “60 Minutes” story. That, between his bearing and his interests, he’s not a natural for TV may have worked in his favor here: Had the Clancy family tragedy happened in a previous era, a true-crime-hungry newsanchor might have pushed harder than Patrick Clancy was willing to go into the gruesome details of the night. (This would’ve been a classic Diane Sawyer or Connie Chung interview, and, as such, might have pushed into more uncomfortable territory.)
	

	What’s been most interesting, to this viewer of the trial from afar, about the story is Patrick’s ability to forgive his ex-wife for what she has admitted to doing to their family. Douthat asked about that: Patrick has forgiven Lindsay, even though she did not ask for it. Were Douthat, perhaps, a more seasoned question-asker on camera, he might have asked how often the two speak and what else passes between them. Douthat let opportunities like this go.

	Regardless, landing this interview is a win for CBS News at an interesting time: The network’s news division, run by former opinion journalist Bari Weiss, has tended toward a thumb-on-scale favoritism toward establishment narratives, even as the establishment itself seems to be tilting toward derangement. On Tony Dokoupil’s first night as “CBS Evening News” anchor, during the U.S. attack on Venezuela that resulted in the capture of that nation’s president, Nicolás Maduro, the “Evening News” featured a lengthy and incurious interview with Pete Hegseth. I was similarly unimpressed — during the debut of Weiss’ newly overhauled “60 Minutes” one week ago — by that episode’s “big get,” Norah O’Donnell’s interview with an Air Force officer shot down over Iran. Taking nothing away from his experience, her questions seemed overly deferent to the U.S. military’s narrative.

	With that in mind, Douthat deserves praise for being genuinely thoughtful and curious about how Patrick Clancy is doing these days. This was the interview every TV outlet sought, and “60 Minutes” can be doubly proud: Its name and heritage may well have helped book the most-talked-about figure of the moment, and its on-camera talent was more open to deep questions than to relitigating the legal case. The question remaining is whether, in weeks between massive gets that exist entirely outside the narrative of an increasingly unpopular presidency whose functionaries Weiss courts, “60 Minutes” can maintain this momentum.

schema.headline: ’60 Minutes’ Patrick Clancy Interview Provides a Surprisingly Thoughtful Take on Much-Watched Trial

title: NYU Langone Privately Bought the Site of a Landmark AMC Theater — New Yorkers Are Now Fighting to Save It
description: “We came to this place for magic.”On a rainy Sunday afternoon, Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal stood in solidarity with more than 100
body:
“We came to this place for magic.”On a rainy Sunday afternoon, Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal stood in solidarity with more than 100 New Yorkers outside AMC Kips Bay 15. In his best Australian accent, he recited Nicole Kidman’s iconic AMC Theatres ad in a loving tribute to the neighborhood’s longstanding cultural institution. But despite a record-breaking summer at the box office, the Kips Bay multiplex is expected to close at the end of this year.


	“I’m a lifelong resident of Kips Bay, and I came out here to support my favorite theater that I’ve been going to since I was a child,” said Lucy Di Lorenzo, one of the many Gen-Zers who attended the protest.
	

	The site of the Kips Bay AMC, the chain’s second-largest multiplex in Manhattan, was privately purchased by NYU Langone over a year ago. But several city officials at the protest told Variety they didn’t learn about the deal until after it had gone through.

	“NYU is a neighbor, and we’ve worked with them in many different capacities, so it was surprising that we had to reach out to them to find out that they were the ones looking to acquire the land behind us,” New York State Sen. Kristen Gonzalez explained after the protest. “It’s not unreasonable to ask NYU to be proactive in engaging with the community.”

	The “Save the Kips Bay AMC Theater Rally” was organized by the Eleanor Roosevelt Independent Democrats, a local political club representing several communities across the Lower East Side, East Village and Midtown East. Judith Gross, the group’s president, says her members are “devastated” by the news but remain hopeful they can get through to AMC Theatres and NYU Langone.

	“I’m hoping AMC and NYU see what we’ve done here,” Gross said. “This neighborhood is not a campus for NYU and its medical offices. We’re guiding the whole community to protest these takeovers of what little community space we have left.”
	

	Several local businesses have joined Gross’ rallying cry, including Paddy Reilly’s Music Bar, the staple Irish pub located just around the corner from AMC Kips Bay. After promoting the protest on social media, the bar offered a free drink to anyone who came in afterward with a selfie from the rally.

	“It’s very important because we have a lot of young people in this neighborhood who love to go to the movie theater,” said Desi Murray, who has owned Paddy Reilly’s for the past three years. “It would be a big loss for the community.”

	Paddy Reilly’s is celebrating its 40th year in business. Inside the bar, several locals mourned the potential loss of a community gathering space that’s been around even longer.

	“We’ve been here since ’73,” a patron named Cesar told his buddies at the bar. He took a sip of Guinness. “There has always been a theater here.”As the pub-goers clamored over how surprisingly funny “Resident Evil” was and how great Robert Pattinson’s Batman is, the fate of their favorite local movie theater remains in limbo. It’s a conflict playing out on a much larger scale with the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, which many of Hollywood’s most prominent voices are arguing would diminish opportunities and resources for creatives.

	“And right here, the same thing is happening,” Gonzalez explained. “We’re getting a big new partner coming in, potentially kicking this out, limiting options to see the movies in our neighborhood. And all we’re asking for, whether it’s in Hollywood or right here in Pittsburgh, is for everyday people to be included and have our voices heard.”In a statement to Variety, NYU Langone has responded to the protests: “NYU Langone is committed to providing high-quality, accessible healthcare to the communities we serve. We have been exploring opportunities to expand clinical services and improve access to care as we continue to see growing demand at our Manhattan campus.When the owner of the Second Avenue property approached us most recently regarding a potential sale, we recognized that the site’s proximity to our hospital could help support those long-term community healthcare needs. The purchase remains under contract and is not expected to close until early next year. Years before NYU Langone was approached about the property, AMC and the landlord entered into a lease granting either party a right to terminate at any time.We will provide updates on our clinical plans when the transaction is finalized.”

schema.headline: NYU Langone Privately Bought the Site of a Landmark AMC Theater — New Yorkers Are Now Fighting to Save It

title: ‘My Hero Academia’ Reworks ‘You Say Run’ Theme With Electric Callboy for 10th Anniversary
description: Toho Co., Ltd. has set a 10th-anniversary version of “You Say Run,” the “My Hero Academia” theme, pairing composer Hayashi Yuki with German band Ele
body:
Toho Co., Ltd. has set a 10th-anniversary version of “You Say Run,” the “My Hero Academia” theme, pairing composer Hayashi Yuki with German band Electric Callboy, with a global release set for Sept. 22.

	The reworked track debuted live at the “My Hero Academia in Concert” show in London on Sept. 20 ahead of the wider rollout. Electric Callboy, known for songs including “Hypa Hypa” and its Babymetal collaboration “Ratatata,” features Kevin Ratajczak and Nico Sallach, who connected with Hayashi after he wrote English lyrics for the anniversary version. Toho’s music team had been looking for international artists who could bring powerful shouts and melodic vocals in keeping with the show’s high-energy tone, which led to the Electric Callboy pairing.
	

	“We are beyond excited to have this opportunity to add our vocals to ‘You Say Run,'” said Ratajczak. “The melody of ‘You Say Run’ is so powerful and uplifting – we just absolutely love this song.”


	Sallach said working on the track was pure fun and a huge honor to collaborate on, adding, “We can’t wait for everyone to hear it! We really hope you’re as excited for it as we are.”

	The new version folds the song’s original orchestral arrangement into Electric Callboy’s blend of EDM and pop hooks, arriving a decade after the anime first premiered. “‘You Say Run,’ one of the signature tracks representing ‘My Hero Academia,’ has been reborn with an unprecedented surge of energy by fusing with the incredible vocals of Electric Callboy,” said Hayashi. “I am deeply honored and thrilled to share this special sound born from the intersection of our shared energy.”
	

	Bones Film also unveiled a new illustration to mark the release, showing Izuku Midoriya (“Deku”) performing a “Smash” in a nod to the cover art of the anime’s original Season 1 soundtrack.

	“I truly hope the song crosses borders and genres, reaches as many hearts as possible, and resonates passionately with everyone,” said Hayashi. “And while the track is absolute perfection, the cover art is top-tier too. Plus Ultra.”

	The release marks a decade since “My Hero Academia” debuted, and the franchise remains among anime’s biggest global hits. Horikoshi Kohei’s manga concluded in August 2024 after selling more than 100 million copies globally, and the anime spans eight seasons, 170+1 episodes and four feature films. The new song is part of the ongoing “My Hero Academia The Animation 10th Anniversary” project, which will continue through 2026 with further announcements on the anniversary’s dedicated website.

	“You Say Run -10th Anniversary Ver.-” by Hayashi Yuki featuring Electric Callboy streams globally and across major platforms starting Sept. 22. 

	“My Hero Academia” is a Japanese anime series based on the manga by Horikoshi Kohei, set in a world where about 80% of the population has a superpowered ability known as a Quirk. It follows Izuku Midoriya and his classmates at U.A. High School as they train to become heroes who protect society from disasters and Quirk-wielding villains. The anime released its eighth and final season in fall 2025.

	Formed in Germany in 2010, Electric Callboy has built a global following on genre-blending hits such as “Hypa Hypa,” “We Got the Moves” and the Babymetal collaboration “Ratatata.” Known for a sound that mixes pop and metalcore, the band is currently building momentum around its new album, “Tanzneid.”

schema.headline: ‘My Hero Academia’ Reworks ‘You Say Run’ Theme With Electric Callboy for 10th Anniversary

title: Guy Gardner Is Back! Nathan Fillion Breaks Down His ‘Lanterns’ Debut and Why He’s the DC Universe’s Main Throughline
description:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for Season 1, Episode 6 of “Lanterns,” now streaming on HBO Max.

	Nathan Fillion has had a hard time
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for Season 1, Episode 6 of “Lanterns,” now streaming on HBO Max.

	Nathan Fillion has had a hard time convincing his friends that he’s actually in “Lanterns” after being absent for the first five episodes.

	“Thank goodness HBO has been kind enough to use my face up on the placard on the screen!” he quips to Variety.

	But after tonight’s episode, Guy Gardner (Fillion) is back in action, revealed to be the new Green Lantern after John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) leaves behind the ring for good. The comedic character, complete with his signature bowl haircut, appears in the 2026 timeline as John returns to Rushville and meets up with Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) one last time before Hal is found dead in the bleachers.

	“It’s nice that there’s a bunch of us witnessing the birth of the DC Universe that’s being thrown at us in these pieces, and Guy Gardner is becoming a thread in the backdrop,” Fillion says. “He’s a very public part. I think that says a lot about who he is.”



	

									Courtesy of John Johnson/HBO
	




	In the episode, Guy visits John in jail after getting the distress signal from Rushville. While Guy is initially reluctant to bust him out, John hits him where it hurts the deepest: “Everything you have is because I didn’t take it.”

	With that, Guy is “beholden” to someone for the first time in his life.

	“Wearing the ring, and having the mantle of Green Lantern, is far more important to Guy’s ego than it is to Hal and John’s. The stakes are higher for his sense of identity,” Fillion says. “He doesn’t like that he owes John Stewart anything — John Stewart needs a favor, and that’s what he leans on.”


	For whoever’s counting, Guy was selected as the third-best Green Lantern option on Earth after Hal and John.


	“I certainly think there’s a chip on Guy’s shoulder, but I think it’s satiated with the fact that he’s the only guy in the room with the ring,” Fillion says. “That status suits Guy very, very well. Guy is a fellow who’s really comfortable throwing his weight around.”
	

	Tied to Guy’s ego is his public persona. The first time audiences see his face in the series isn’t in the prison scene with John, but a cardboard cut-out advertising Electro Punch in the local grocery store.



	

									Courtesy of John Johnson/HBO
	



	“Guy is very concerned about brand and corporate sponsorship, he has financial goals. He wants to open a bar, he has retirement plans; he’s not a dummy. I think he’s TikTok literate, he understands trends. I think he’s done more than one dance or two,” Fillion says with a laugh. “That’s part of his schtick. He wants to not just be Green Lantern, but a famous Green Lantern.”

	Fillion admits he was surprised when he got the call to reprise the character in “Lanterns,” a much more grounded show than Guy usually fits the mold for.

	“My concern was consistency. I knew there was going to be a shift in tone. What I didn’t want was for there to be a shift in the character himself,” Fillion says. “So I just likened it much to, if you were to spend a weekend in Metropolis, or spend a weekend in Gotham — you’d be the same person, but you’d have very different weekends.”
	

	Fillion grew up reading comic books and, long before the current reconception of the DC Universe, he was a voice actor in the mid-aughts Cartoon Network series “Justice League Unlimited.” (Fillion, beloved to genre fans as the lead of the brilliant-but-canceled sci-fi series “Firefly,” also voiced characters in “Deadpool & Wolverine” and “Guardians of the Galaxy.”)

	“We collected secondhand comic books in stacks about two feet high, and it was a real mishmash across the board. But I got a real, solid knowledge base about pretty much everything DC, Marvel. I confess I didn’t see the value of Guy Gardner back then,” Fillion says. “I, like many people, disliked Guy Gardner. I think we’re kind of supposed to dislike him.”



	

					Nathan Fillion in “Superman”
									Courtesy of DC Studios
	



	When tasked with introducing Guy in James Gunn’s “Superman” movie, which was released in summer 2025, he had to “dig deep” to tell the character’s story.

	“Because we haven’t delved into his particular past in any great detail, I’m able to go through his history and cherry pick what I want to pull from to portray the character. For me, he’s this tremendous jerk — he has to have a reason to be a jerk,” Fillion says. “The idea that he was at one point passed up, the way he was raised, his relationship with his father wasn’t tremendous. So he has this need to prove himself. He’s fearless in that way.”

	One example Fillion points to from the comics is when Guy was hit by a bus and spent time in a coma. “The coma is what flipped that switch for Guy Gardner,” he says. “I think he has a little bit of brain damage.”

	“Lanterns” is just one piece of the quickly expanding DC Universe under co-chairmen Gunn and Peter Safran. As for the underperformance of this summer’s “Supergirl” in comparison to “Superman,” Fillion says: “I can’t tell you much as far as to how people responded. I can tell you, though, how I respond. I really enjoy when the right person is selected for the right job.”

	“Milly Alcock, I think her take on Supergirl is brilliant, I am so pleased with these favorite characters of mine coming to life,” Fillion continues. “I have yet to be disappointed by anything James Gunn does, which is great because he puts me in most everything he does!”

	In fact, Fillion and Gunn’s creative collaboration goes all the way back to 2006’s “Slither” and 2010’s “Super,” long before Gunn took over the reins of the MCU’s “Guardians of the Galaxy” and, later, the future of the DC Universe. This “Lanterns” episode marks just the first encounter between Guy and John, who are both set to appear in “Man of Tomorrow,” Gunn’s follow-up to “Superman,” which will release in 2027.
	

	“Within this secret club of the superhero community, there is yet another layer of secret club, the Green Lantern community,” Fillion teases about the highly anticipated blockbuster. “It delves one club deeper than the rest of, let’s call them the Justice Gang.”

	As for how “Lanterns” fits into the larger DC Universe, the show’s grounded approach is creating new inroads.



	

									Courtesy of John Johnson/HBO
	



	“Up to this point, we’ve been given the idea, ‘What if we took Batman out of that universe and put him into our world? What if it was real in our world?’” Fillion says. “James Gunn’s universe is, ‘What if we lived in that universe, the comic book universe where giant monsters appear, where there’s robots and where there’s fantastic happenings constantly?’”

	“This concept is new to us, and I’m really enjoying watching it unfold as a universe,” he continues. “We’ve spent a week in Metropolis, and now we’re going to Middle America. We’re going to farm country. I’m so anxiously awaiting a dip into Gotham.”

	Guy will also soon be seen in the animated show “Mister Miracle,” which Fillion has already recorded the voiceover for. As Fillion puts it, it’s a natural extension of how anybody living in the DC Universe would be “inundated” with the character while walking around town and driving by billboards.

	“It’s really exciting for me, personally, because I think I hold the record for most characters portrayed in the MCU, and now I hold the record for the most projects by a DCU character,” he says. “This is a nice place to be. I’m in the catbird seat.”

schema.headline: Guy Gardner Is Back! Nathan Fillion Breaks Down His ‘Lanterns’ Debut and Why He’s the DC Universe’s Main Throughline

title: Charlize Theron on ‘The Odyssey’ Becoming Universal’s Highest-Grossing Movie and Raising Millions to Fight Femicide in Africa With CTAOP
description:
Last week, Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” became Universal Pictures’ highest-grossing film of all time, grossing $1.68 billion and counting. 

	“
body:
Last week, Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” became Universal Pictures’ highest-grossing film of all time, grossing $1.68 billion and counting. 

	“I feel like I got a great invitation to the best party in town, and I don’t know how I got it, but I’m really glad I got invited,” Oscar winner Charlize Theron told Variety on Saturday night. (For the record, Theron stars in two of the studio’s top 10 movies, with 2017’s “Fate of the Furious” coming in at No. 6.)
	

	But the box office milestone wasn’t really the figure Theron had at the top of her mind. She was more focused on how much money she could raise for her foundation, the Charlize Theron Africa Outreach Program — which works to strengthen the health and safety of youth in Southern Africa. CTAOP hosted its 6th annual block party on the Universal backlot with a guest list that included January Jones, Nick Kroll, Patton Oswald, Skye P. Marshall, Jeannie Mai, Heather Gay, Natalie Martinez, chef Andrew Zimmern, Thaddeus LaGrone, Aggy K. Adams, Shudu Musida, Naledi Masilo, Michelle De Leon, Max Talisman, as well as NBCUniversal Entertainment chairman Donna Langley. 


	“Universal truly is my family,” Theron said. “I owe so much to Donna Langley, and to Michael Moses and Peter Cramer. All of them have stood by me for my entire career.”

	Speaking of family, Theron is also expected to reprise her role as the villainous Cipher in “Fast Forever,” the final installment of the “Fast and Furious” franchise. Vin Diesel declared the film’s script is “the best [he’s] read in decades,” but he hasn’t shared a copy with Theron yet. “He’s very secretive,” she explained.
	

	But what would a happy ending look like for someone like Cipher? 

	“That is a difficult thing,” Theron said, pondering the character’s fate. “She’s a tricky bitch. She’s messy. I don’t know. I’m sure Vin will come up with a great way for her to … I almost said die, but I guess she doesn’t have to die, right?” (With a spinoff series in the works at Peacock, it’s safe to say any fate is possible for the massive ensemble cast.)



	

					Kid Cudi and Charlize Theron attend Charlize Theron’s Africa Outreach Program’s annual block party.
									Getty Images for CTAOP
	





	

					January Jones and Charlize Theron
									Getty Images for CTAOP
	



	Now back to the topic at hand: next year, CTAOP will turn 20 and, to date, has served over 80 organizations, reached over 4.8 million youth and granted $16.5 million to local grassroots organizations.

	“The success of CTAOP is understanding the importance of a community here — because without this community, other communities on the ground can’t do the work,” Theron said about CTAOP’s supporters.

	“It’s also just good for the soul to see that people care,” she continued. “It’s such a misconception that Americans don’t care about what’s going on in the rest of the world. If anything, I think they do. There’s a big percentage of the population that understands that less than 1% of [America’s] overall budget going to foreign aid and saving millions and millions of lives is a good thing. And I really hope we can get back to those times, because people are dying.”

	Here, Theron grew particularly impassioned, explaining that people try to oversimplify the situation. “The truth is, we’re taking so many steps back,” she said. “To not think that all of this is going to affect us in the long term makes it hard to not see the geopolitical side of it. If you take away the humanitarian out of it — what’s important to you? Is it the safety of wanting to know that you’re safe here in America? Then you should care about other people as well.”

	As CTAOP works toward that 20th anniversary, Theron said her “ridiculous hope and dream is to say we don’t have to do this anymore. It’s solved. But I don’t think that that’s going to be the case.”

	“If anything,” she explained, “I think we’re leaning into a year where we really have to spend real money toward organizations that really, really work on the ground with gender-based violence. The femicide happening in South Africa right now is beyond brutal.” 
	

	The horrors for women and girls are prevalent everywhere, Theron said, but her native South Africa is particularly devastated by it. 

	“Every morning, I get on my feed and I hear of another young woman’s body that was found in a dump in East Rand, where I grew up. And it’s like nobody cares. Nobody’s talking about these things,” Theron added, growing impassioned. “The value of women’s lives should matter. And when you find a young woman’s body in a dump, that should be the most important thing that we’re talking about.”

	Scroll for a look inside the starry celebration, which raised more than $1 million for the organization.

title: China Box Office: ‘Once Upon a Time in the Middle East’ Secures Sixth Weekend at No. 1 in Sluggish Frame
description: Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East” retained its grip on the top spot at the mainland China box office for the six
body:
Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East” retained its grip on the top spot at the mainland China box office for the sixth consecutive weekend, taking in RMB28.1 million ($4.1 million) over the Sept. 18–20 frame, according to data from Artisan Gateway. 

	Directed by Wen Muye (“Dying to Survive”) and starring Shen Teng, Jiang Qiming, Aarif Rahman, and Omar Sherif, the hit feature has pushed its cumulative haul to $325.7 million since launching nationwide on Aug. 11. The narrative centers on a debt-strapped Chinese chef whose restaurant in a fictional Middle Eastern city becomes an unexpected sanctuary for local civilians and orphans when armed conflict breaks out.
	

	Pearl River Film Group’s crime thriller “V” took second place in its fifth weekend, adding $2.8 million to lift its gross to $89.6 million. Directed by Han Yan (“Love Never Ends”), the gritty drama features an ensemble cast led by Tony Ka Fai Leung, Zhu Yilong, Tan Jianci, and Kara Wai, following an ambitious man whose rapid ascent to power is shadowed by dark, lingering fallout.


	Universal’s “The Odyssey” climbed back into third position, collecting $1.9 million in its fifth weekend. The epic has amassed $106.5 million across mainland theaters. 

	Pearl Studio’s animated fantasy comedy “All Wishes Come True!” moved to fourth place in its tenth frame, generating $1.7 million. Directed by Mu Zhengyang, the enduring mythological feature now has a cumulative total of $286.3 million.

	Sony’s superhero spectacle “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” re-entered the top five, pulling in $800,000 in its eighth weekend and has lifted its cume to $232.5 million since rolling out on July 29, maintaining its status as the year’s top-earning international import in the territory.
	

	Mainland China’s overall weekend grosses dropped to a quiet $15 million amid a pre-holiday lull ahead of the forthcoming National Day corridor. The 2026 year-to-date box office stands at $4.29 billion, down 29.2% compared to the same period in 2025

title: Paramount Settlement Talks Progress but AGs Push for Tougher Terms
description: On Sunday, settlement talks between Paramount and the state attorneys general that sued to block its Warner Bros. Discovery deal continued — but the
body:
On Sunday, settlement talks between Paramount and the state attorneys general that sued to block its Warner Bros. Discovery deal continued — but there was no resolution by the end of the day. 

	But while California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who is leading the 12-state coalition’s antitrust litigation, is said to be open to considering a set of conditions that would put certain restrictions on Paramount’s takeover of Warner Bros., at least two other AGs are pushing for stricter measures before they sign off on anything.
	

	Over the weekend, the sides hashed out potential terms of a settlement. The sides were expected to put the negotiations on hiatus on Monday for the Yom Kippur holiday.


	The terms discussed were said to include Paramount agreeing to operate Warner Bros.’ studio operations separately for a time (something Paramount chief David Ellison already said he was willing to do). Also on the table was a requirement that the merged Paramount-Warner Bros. release at least 30 films theatrically per year (a promise Ellison has already made, repeatedly), with financial penalties if they fail to hit that mark. In addition, the two sides also discussed a binding guarantee from Paramount that it would not relocate its existing California operations (as Ellison has threatened to do) and the formation of a third-party “editorial adviser” to oversee CNN and CBS News.

	But some of the states want more.

	New York Attorney General Letitia James, for one, wants Paramount to commit to specific job-protection guarantees, including for employees at Warner Bros., sources confirmed. Paramount has claimed it would achieve $6 billion in cost savings by merging with WBD — and that would imply thousands of layoffs.
	

	In addition, Connecticut Attorney General William Tong is opposed to the current proposed settlement terms with Paramount, Variety confirmed. A source familiar with the AG’s position said he wants any agreement to include stronger provisions guaranteeing that CNN and CBS News remain independent from interference from Paramount’s owners, with more teeth than a third-party “adviser.” Details of the pushback by the New York and Connecticut AGs has been previously reported by CNN and the media industry newsletter Status.

	Bonta’s office on Sunday evening provided the same comment it did when word of the “advanced” settlement talks emerged Friday: AG spox: “Potential settlement talks are confidential. We cannot confirm or deny whether settlement talks are occurring or their alleged substance.”

	The battle has taken on political overtones given the connections of Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison and his family to President Donald Trump. The Justice Department and FCC have approved the transaction without asking for any concessions or remedies — an unusually hands-off approach for such a large horizontal merger. That opened the door for the 12 states to flex their legal muscle to scrutinize the combination.

	David Ellison has voiced his belief, which is shared by other critics of the AGs’ legal maneuver, that the opposition to Paramount-WBD is about his control CNN — rather than antitrust concerns. “I believe this fight is not really about market share,” Ellison wrote in a New York Times op-ed. “I believe a plainer worry sits beneath the briefs and the news releases: the news. The issue is whether I can be trusted as a steward of Warner’s CNN.” Ellison has pledged that CNN and CBS News journalists “will continue to answer to the facts and to all the people they serve — not to any party or cause.”

	The lawsuit filed by the 12 states and a similar antitrust case filed by the Writers Guild of America West are the last obstacles holding up Paramount’s closing of the WBD acquisition. It’s been a wild, yearlong chase that included Paramount having to outbid Netflix, which reached a deal to buy Warner Bros. and HBO n early December. The streaming giant was out of the picture by late February.

	Even if Paramount is able to reach a settlement with the state AGs, the Paramount-WB merger will not close immediately, a knowledgeable source told Variety. Because of the $110 billion pact’s intricate financing — including some $24 billion from Middle Eastern government funds — and other factors, Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will need at least a week or so after any deal with the states is in place.
	

	Tong, after the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California granted the states’ request for a temporary restraining order halting the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger in July, said in an official statement: “This is a critical victory for American consumers, for objective and independent journalism, and for the workers, actors, artists and fans of our country’s celebrated film and television industry. We are suing to protect free and fair competition, choice and quality programming. This order demonstrates the strength of our case and the power of states stepping in to fill the void left by Trump’s absent Department of Justice.”

	And New York’s James, after the 12 states initially filed their lawsuit in July, said in a statement: “For over a century, Paramount and Warner Bros. have competed to create movies and television that bring people together, inspire and sustain generations of artists, and help us understand the world. This merger would destroy that competition, creating a massive company with unprecedented power and influence over news and entertainment across the globe. Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. threatens to raise costs for consumers and put jobs and businesses nationwide at risk.”

	Gene Maddaus contributed to this report.

title: Ash Trevino Files Defamation Lawsuit Against TikToker Who She Claims Called Probation Officer
description:
Influencer Ash Trevino
                          Someone Called My Probation Officer With B.S.!!!
body:
Influencer Ash Trevino
                          Someone Called My Probation Officer With B.S.!!!
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Influencer star Ash Trevino has filed a lawsuit against a woman she says called her probation officer in the hopes that the influencer would get a violation of her supervised release ... before posting the whole recorded call on her TikTok.
      
    
            In a Sept. 17 filing ... Ash's legal team claimed that Raelene Ortega called her probation officer ... and alleged that the influencer was "making threats" and using "racial slurs" online against a restaurant she claimed Trevino had publicly criticized.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            When the officer told her she could report any illegal activities to the police, the filing -- which lists Stephanie Lama as a co-defendant -- claims Raelene said ... "OK, but, that's no[t] like violation of her, of her probation?"
      

            According to the docs, Raelene also told the officer that she had screenshots and screen recordings of Ash "making those threats."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Afterward ... Ash says Raelene uploaded the entire call to her TikTok.
      
    
            Meanwhile, Ash denies ever making threats or racial slurs and claims the defendants made knowingly false claims directly to her probation officer in the hopes she'd receive a probation violation.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            We reported earlier ... Ash avoided jail time following her fraud charges, and was instead ordered to 2 years of community supervision, 120 hours of community service, an anti-theft program and financial counseling.
      
    
            As part of her deal to stay out of jail ... Ash was also told not to take any alcohol and illegal drugs, frequent strip clubs and liquor stores, and unless she received permission, travel 100 miles from her Texas home.
      
    
            Ash -- who prosecutors claimed had relationships with 50-75 inmates -- also was ordered to avoid any romantic entanglements with anyone with a criminal record.

            See how they run!!! It seems the highly anticipated series of Beatles biopics will depict the iconic opening of "A Hard Day's Night" ... and we have the photos.
      
    
            Harris Dickinson, Joseph Quinn and Barry Keoghan were spotted being chased down the streets at London's Marylebone Station ... recreating the moment when their respective characters John Lennon, George Harrison and Ringo Starr ran away from their own adoring fans for the 1964 film.
      
    
            The trio could be seen smiling, dancing and ... well ... running like their lives depended on it.
      

            Doing the chase was a dozen extras or so ... in convincing '60s attire.
      
    
            Of course, the only Beatle missing was Paul Mescal's Paul McCartney.

title: Carrot Top's Alleged Extortionist Responds to Lawsuit
description:
Carrot Top
                          Man Accused of Extorting Comedian
body:
Carrot Top
                          Man Accused of Extorting Comedian
                          Denies Being Responsible For His Suicide Attempt
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 20, 2026
                
                            10:05 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 20, 2026
                                12:28 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The man who Carrot Top's legal team claims tried to extort the comedian with a sexually explicit recording is speaking out ... and he claims he never threatened to release the video ahead of his suicide attempt.
      
    
            In response to the Sept. 3 filing ... Brian Evans tells TMZ ... that the USB drive recording the lawsuit mentions had already been deleted.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            He tells TMZ ... "I never threatened - ever - to post any video anywhere in exchange for a settlement. … The video they are discussing - as I made very clear - was deleted a long time ago in accordance with the prior settlement."
      

            Brian said of the situation with Carrot Top -- whose real name is Scott Thompson -- that he was "sorry that Scott apparently did something to hurt himself."
      
    
            He added ... "I do not consider Scott to be a bad person ... based on what I know - but he made a few decisions that were not good ones. That is not a reason to hurt himself."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            He went on to say ... "Finally, it’s not my fault … that Scott did what he did. We don’t even actually know what he did. He survived and I am glad about that. Scott is still young and has a big life ahead of him. It’s not my intent to bring this guy down. It’s the opposite." Page Six was the first to report on this story.
      
    
            We reported earlier ... the 61-year-old's attorney claims Brian said he would enter the alleged recording into a court's legal docket ... unless CT's legal team forked over $500,000 in a settlement payment.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As for Carrot Top ... the prop-based comedian remains hospitalized following his suicide attempt Friday.
      
    
            If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat 988lifeline.org.

body:
Tender Fest 2026
                          Lizzo, Puka Nacua, Kyren Williams, and Other Celebs
                          Attend World's Only Chicken Tender Festival
                      
      
    
            The 5th annual Tender Fest took place this weekend in Beverly Hills, and two things it was not short of were chicken tenders and celebrities! 
      
    
            Yes, a food festival solely featuring chicken tenders does exist and we were front and center for the festivities. The event featured vendors from all over the country, including Tender Crush, Pizzeria Mozza, Raising Cane’s, Delilah, Dave’s Hot Chicken, and con-tender competition winner and popular LA Thai restaurant, Jitlada. 
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Lizzo, who was a judge for this year's con-tender competition -- a face-off between local LA Chefs -- spoke to us and told us what she thinks goes into the perfect chicken tender. 
      

        
                    
                  
      
    
            Sitcom icon Jaleel White hosted the event and we spoke to him about his show "Flip Side" and asked if he would ever go on a show like "The Traitors" … watch the clip to see if he would answer the call. 
      
    
            Other Judges on the panel this year included LA Rams stars Puka Nacua and Kyren Williams, Chef Cat Cora, and food influencer Kevin Noparvar. Other stars in attendance included Alana Haim, 'Impaulsive' co-host Mike Majlak, and WWE star Cathy Kelley. 
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Tender Fest comes to Chicago next on October 10th.
